source_name: The Region (connectingregion.com) — Adria Business News & Intelligence
why_relevant: English-language Adria-wide business intelligence portal with country desks; observed article 'Aleksandar Kostić's AIK Banka Acquires Montenegro's Hipotekarna Banka'. Explicitly regional-aggregator positioning, useful as both a direct source and a pointer to underlying local reports.

source_name: MontenegroBusiness.eu
why_relevant: English-language Montenegro business portal aimed at a regional/foreign-investor readership; observed piece explicitly framing 'Montenegro's banking sector enters consolidation phase' around Hipotekarna banka and AIK Group's ~80% control via AikGroup (CY) Limited. Good for consolidation/integration narrative and ownership-structure detail in English.

source_name: Monte.business (Montenegro Business)
why_relevant: Second English-language Montenegro business portal with analytical pieces on the banking landscape and 'the rise of private financial market players'. Indirect: rarely breaks appointments, but maps the actor set (which owners/groups are active), which feeds the actor map for leadership tracking.

source_name: Kamatica — tag 'spajanje banaka' (Serbian finance portal)
why_relevant: Serbian retail-finance portal maintaining a persistent topical tag for bank mergers ('spajanje banaka'). A ready-made, low-cost pointer feed for merger/integration items across the region, including Serbian owners' Montenegrin operations; tag pages snowball into further outlets and deal names.

source_name: Nova.rs — Biznis
why_relevant: Serbian news portal that reports parent-group bank executive appointments ('Vlastimir Vuković na čelu Komercijalne banke'). Indirect for Montenegro: Serbian-owned groups (NLB Komercijalna, AIK/Agri Europe) drive subsidiary board composition in Podgorica, so parent-level appointments are a leading indicator.

source_name: Dnevne novine DAN — Ekonomija (Serbian-language Montenegrin daily, Serb-community/regional register)
why_relevant: Podgorica daily published in Serbian and heavily read/syndicated across the Serbian-language regional space; observed 'Kostićeva firma kupuje crnogorsku Hipotekarnu banku'. Sits at the seam between the Montenegrin and regional Serbian-language channel and is often the text regional portals re-run.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters — Banking & Finance in Montenegro (comparative guide)
why_relevant: Regional (CEE/SEE) legal-market publisher whose Montenegro banking chapter is authored by local counsel; explains the governance framework (e.g. two-tier management/supervisory board regime) that determines what 'leadership change' filings look like, and identifies law firms advising on the bank M&A deals — a pointer to deal actors.

source_name: NLB Group – Press releases (Media Center)
why_relevant: NLB d.d. Ljubljana is the parent of NLB Banka AD Podgorica. Group-level press releases routinely announce subsidiary management-board appointments, reorganisations and market moves, and are published in English before local Montenegrin statements.

source_name: NLB Group – Investor news (regulated IR disclosures)
why_relevant: Regulated inside-information and IR announcements of a Ljubljana/London-listed issuer. Supervisory-board and subsidiary governance changes, and M&A affecting Montenegro (e.g. the 2026 Addiko takeover attempt), surface here first, in English.

source_name: SEOnet – Ljubljana Stock Exchange disclosure portal (NLB issuer feed)
why_relevant: Statutory disclosure venue for NLB d.d. under the Ljubljana Stock Exchange Rules and the Slovenian Market in Financial Instruments Act. Acts as the authoritative timestamped feed of NLB announcements, including supervisory-board decisions that precede subsidiary CEO changes in Podgorica.

source_name: NLB Group – Careers / job openings portal
why_relevant: Group-level vacancy aggregation across NLB markets; Montenegro postings (NLB Banka Podgorica, ~650 staff) reveal hiring waves, new functions and reorganisations before any announcement.

source_name: Erste Group Bank AG – Press releases
why_relevant: Erste Group owns Erste Bank AD Podgorica (4th largest bank in Montenegro, ~13.8% share). Group press room is the English-first channel for management appointments and structural changes at the Montenegrin subsidiary.

source_name: Erste Group Bank AG – Careers / positions offered
why_relevant: Group job portal covering subsidiaries; Erste Bank Podgorica (~420 staff) roles posted here indicate hiring, new departments and relocations of group functions into/out of Montenegro.

source_name: Addiko Bank AG – News / ad-hoc announcements
why_relevant: Addiko Bank AG (Vienna-listed, ECB/FMA supervised) is parent of Addiko Bank AD Podgorica. Its 'organizational update' releases explicitly name subsidiary executive-board changes (e.g. the 30 Jul 2026 release covering the AG Supervisory Board and Addiko Serbia Executive Board) — the same template is used for Montenegro.

source_name: Addiko Bank AG – Management Board / banking network pages (roster baseline)
why_relevant: Canonical current-state roster of group management and the six subsidiary banks (incl. Montenegro). Diffing this page over time is a cheap, high-precision detector of leadership changes even when no press release is issued.

source_name: pressetext / PTA ad-hoc distribution archive (Austrian issuers: Addiko, Erste)
why_relevant: PTA is the distributor Addiko Bank AG uses for PTA-News / PTA-AFR / PTA-DD releases under the Austrian BörseG. Gives a machine-readable, timestamped feed of Austrian-parent disclosures that mention Montenegrin subsidiaries — often earlier than the corporate website's own index refresh.

source_name: Wiener Börse – Addiko Bank AG issuer page (AT000ADDIKO0)
why_relevant: Exchange-side issuer page linking company news and mandatory publications for the Austrian parent of Addiko Bank Podgorica; useful as an independent cross-check that a disclosure exists and when.

source_name: OTP Group – Investor relations announcements
why_relevant: OTP Bank Nyrt. is parent of Crnogorska komercijalna banka (CKB), the largest bank in Montenegro. Group announcements cover subsidiary governance, mergers and senior appointments; CKB CEOs have historically been OTP-seconded Hungarians whose appointment is a group decision.

source_name: Budapest Stock Exchange (BÉT) – OTP Bank issuer publications
why_relevant: OTP states it fulfils disclosure obligations on its own site, on bet.hu and on kozzetetelek.mnb.hu. The exchange feed is the authoritative timestamped mirror for OTP announcements touching the Montenegrin subsidiary.

source_name: MNB kozzetetelek.mnb.hu – Hungarian statutory capital-market publications (OTP)
why_relevant: Regulator-run statutory publication site named by OTP as a mandatory disclosure venue. Independent of OTP's own web estate, so it survives site redesigns and is the hardest-to-suppress copy of an announcement affecting CKB Montenegro.

source_name: OTP Bank – Montenegro market page (group Global Securities Services / country page)
why_relevant: Group-maintained English country page describing the Montenegrin operation; useful for baseline entity facts, official English naming of CKB, and occasional structural updates.

source_name: AIK Banka a.d. Beograd / AikGroup – corporate news (parent of Hipotekarna banka Podgorica)
why_relevant: AikGroup (Kostić) completed the acquisition of 74.9% of Hipotekarna banka AD Podgorica (~EUR 75m, EUR 9.77/share) in 2025 after CBCG and competition-authority approvals. This is a newly foreign-owned Montenegrin bank whose board changes will now be driven from Belgrade — a channel not covered by the traditional NLB/Erste/OTP set.

source_name: Belgrade Stock Exchange (Belex) – AIK Banka issuer disclosures
why_relevant: AIK Banka is a Belgrade-listed issuer; its statutory disclosures are the formal venue for announcing acquisitions and governance changes at Hipotekarna banka Podgorica. Serbian-language regulatory channel that English-only monitoring misses entirely.

source_name: Ziraat Bankası – Subsidiaries abroad / corporate pages (parent of Ziraat Bank Montenegro AD Podgorica)
why_relevant: Ziraat Bank Montenegro AD Podgorica is a wholly-owned Turkish state-bank subsidiary (licensed 2015, ~1.34% market share). The parent's English subsidiary pages and integrated annual reports are the group-level record of the Montenegrin unit's structure and senior appointments.

source_name: KAP – Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu (Turkish public disclosure platform), Ziraat entities
why_relevant: Turkey's statutory disclosure platform. Ziraat group debt issuers file here; board and subsidiary changes appear as structured filings. Hypothesised as the earliest formal channel for Ziraat Bank Montenegro governance changes, though Ziraat Bankası's unlisted-equity status limits coverage.

source_name: Alta banka a.d. Beograd / Alta Pay Group – Serbian owner group web presence
why_relevant: Alta Pay Group holds ~76% of Alta banka (Belgrade) and is repeatedly named in the run brief as a regional owner relevant to Montenegro. Its Serbian-language corporate communications are the group-level channel for any Montenegrin banking-entity governance move.

source_name: Lovćen banka AD Podgorica – Obavještenja za akcionare (shareholder notices)
why_relevant: Shareholder-notice page of a Montenegrin bank with regional ownership. Shareholder-assembly convocations and their agendas are where board (odbor direktora) elections and dismissals are disclosed in Montenegrin before any group-level English statement — the local mirror of the group channel this cell tracks.
